$comment: One fixture, asserted by both the Go server and the web client. Each entry is an input a real caller has sent or plausibly will, and the canonical domain it must resolve to. If either language drifts, its own test suite fails -- which is the check that did not exist when `kind=movies` quietly matched nothing for weeks.
$comment_unknown: An unrecognised name must resolve to nothing, and callers read that as 'no filter'. Returning a value nothing matches is how a filter becomes indistinguishable from an outage.
$comment_pairs: Spellings that must be treated as the same domain. The audio/music pair is the one that matters operationally: cards cached before this vocabulary carry 'audio' while new clients send 'music'.
$comment_distinct: Must NOT collide. Comics sit inside the book category range at the provider level, so filing them together is an easy and costly mistake.
